title: "Glossary"

{{< include _includes/lang-switcher/glossary.en.qmd >}}


Every journey collects new words. Some are friendly on first meeting, such as *caffeine* and *ritual*. Others arrive packed tight, such as *HPA axis* and *error-related negativity*, as if five ideas were folded into one suitcase.

This page unpacks those suitcases. When a chapter uses a technical word, look it up here for a one-sentence definition in everyday English. The chapter numbers point to where the term matters most in the story.

You do not need to memorize the whole table. When you start a new chapter, skim the “By chapter” list at the bottom. Ultra-niche lab constants and diffusion equations are left out on purpose. If you need the primary papers, see the [Bibliography](bibliography.qmd).

Think of this as a pocket phrasebook for the four chapters—not a second textbook.

For a first mug, and for true tea versus herbal drinks, use **[Tea basics](tea-basics.qmd)**. For the longer name sheet—Chinese, Japanese, and Western labels, grades, and teapot words—use **[Tea labels](tea-labels.qmd)**. This glossary stays with chapter jargon only.

## Terms (simple definitions)


| Term | Simple definition | Where it shows up |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="adenosine-receptors">Adenosine receptors (A1, A2A)</span> | Brain “slow down / sleep” sensors that caffeine blocks so you stay awake. | [Chapter 2](modules/module-02/index.qmd) |
| <span id="alpha-brainwaves">Alpha brainwaves</span> | Slower calm-focus brain rhythms (about 8–12 Hz), often linked with L-theanine. | [Chapter 2](modules/module-02/index.qmd) |
| <span id="anterior-insular-cortex">Anterior insular cortex</span> | Brain area that handles both body temperature and feelings like trust or empathy. | [Chapter 4](modules/module-04/index.qmd) |
| <span id="bart">Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART)</span> | Computer game that measures risk-taking by how far people pump a virtual balloon. | [Chapter 5](modules/module-05/index.qmd) |
| <span id="beta-brainwaves">Beta brainwaves</span> | Faster alert (or anxious) brain rhythms (about 12–30 Hz), often up with caffeine. | [Chapter 2](modules/module-02/index.qmd) |
| <span id="assamica">*Camellia sinensis* var. *assamica*</span> | Large-leaf, tropical tea type; often higher caffeine and stronger bitterness. | [Chapter 1](modules/module-01/index.qmd) |
| <span id="sinensis">*Camellia sinensis* var. *sinensis*</span> | Small-leaf, cold-hardier China type; often richer in L-theanine and aroma. | [Chapter 1](modules/module-01/index.qmd) |
| <span id="canton-system">Canton System</span> | Qing rule (1757–1842) that funneled Western trade through Canton and demanded silver payment. | [Chapter 3](modules/module-03/index.qmd) |
| <span id="chanyuan-qinggui">*Chanyuan Qinggui*</span> | Chan monastic rulebook (1103) that set formal tea routines for discipline and wakefulness. | [Chapter 3](modules/module-03/index.qmd) |
| <span id="dual-process-theory">Dual-process theory</span> | Idea that decisions use fast gut thinking (System 1) and slow careful thinking (System 2). | [Chapter 5](modules/module-05/index.qmd) |
| <span id="egcg">EGCG</span> | The standout catechin in green tea; a large share of green tea’s polyphenols. | [Chapter 1](modules/module-01/index.qmd) |
| <span id="embodied-cognition">Embodied cognition</span> | The claim that body feelings (like warmth) can shape social judgments. | [Chapter 4](modules/module-04/index.qmd) |
| <span id="ern">Error-related negativity (ERN)</span> | A quick brain “oops” signal after mistakes; rituals can blunt it. | [Chapter 4](modules/module-04/index.qmd) |
| <span id="hrv">Heart rate variability (HRV)</span> | How much the time between heartbeats varies; higher often means calmer control. | [Chapter 2](modules/module-02/index.qmd) |
| <span id="hpa-axis">HPA axis</span> | The body’s main stress-hormone loop (brain → pituitary → adrenals). | [Chapter 2](modules/module-02/index.qmd) |
| <span id="igt">Iowa Gambling Task (IGT)</span> | Card game that tests learning from long-run gains and losses. | [Chapter 5](modules/module-05/index.qmd) |
| <span id="kissa-yojoki">*Kissa Yōjōki*</span> | Eisai’s 1211 essay promoting tea for health and alertness. | [Chapter 3](modules/module-03/index.qmd) |
| <span id="loss-aversion-lambda">Loss-aversion coefficient (λ)</span> | How much more painful losses feel than equal gains; above 1 means loss-averse. | [Chapter 5](modules/module-05/index.qmd) |
| <span id="l-theanine">L-Theanine</span> | A calming amino acid found in tea that supports relaxed focus. | [Chapter 1](modules/module-01/index.qmd) |
| <span id="ppo">Polyphenol oxidase (PPO)</span> | Leaf enzyme that darkens crushed tea by oxidizing catechins (key to black tea). | [Chapter 1](modules/module-01/index.qmd) |
| <span id="present-bias">Present-bias parameter</span> | How strongly someone prefers rewards *now* over better rewards later. | [Chapter 5](modules/module-05/index.qmd) |
| <span id="scr">Skin conductance response (SCR)</span> | Tiny sweat changes that track stress and arousal. | [Chapter 2](modules/module-02/index.qmd) |
| <span id="theaflavins">Theaflavins</span> | Bright golden-red pigments formed while black tea oxidizes. | [Chapter 1](modules/module-01/index.qmd) |
| <span id="thearubigins">Thearubigins</span> | Darker, larger pigments that give black tea body and color. | [Chapter 1](modules/module-01/index.qmd) |
| <span id="theta-brainwaves">Theta brainwaves</span> | Slower drowsy rhythms (about 4–8 Hz), often up with fatigue or alcohol. | [Chapter 2](modules/module-02/index.qmd) |
| <span id="treaty-of-nanking">Treaty of Nanking (1842)</span> | Unequal treaty ending the First Opium War: indemnity, five ports, Hong Kong ceded. | [Chapter 3](modules/module-03/index.qmd) |
